_comment: Spike fixture, the subchart case (sb-7s2). Same adaptations as the other
two documents: '_comment' keys are additive and not part of the ADR-0001
node shape or envelope, and the file is pretty-printed rather than
canonical.
Shape: 11 blocks, maximum nesting depth 6 (root = depth 1). Every datamodel
path named in a param or a run resolves in ../datamodel.json.
Why this document exists: core.subchart needs a parent chart to sit in, and
it needs the chart it references to be a document the shell can actually
open. Both fixture documents that already ship are candidates for the
reference; this one picks the signup wizard, because an invited teammate
completing the ordinary signup flow is the honest reading of a child chart
- the parent hands off, waits, and carries on.
THREE block types here are PROPOSED and not shipped, all in js/proposed-
core.js: core.subchart (blk_si_invitee_signup, the point of the fixture),
core.foreach (blk_si_each_invitee, added by sb-9nn), and core.invoke /
core.raise, which the failure subtree reuses. The
subchart's on_error slot is core.invoke's, unchanged - the same slot, the
same failure rail vocabulary (sb-68b), the same D13 ruling that an outcome
path is a slot and never a port.
The raise in the failure subtree is caught by the rail of the group the
subchart sits in, exactly as in signup-wizard.json: the two are not joined
by an edge, they name the same event.

config.label: While an invitee is signing up

_comment: The proposed core.foreach (sb-9nn), added by wrapping the
subchart that was already here rather than by inventing a
second subtree beside it. That is the honest reading of the
document's own sentence: the signup wizard runs FOR EACH
invitee, and before this block the only way to author that
was to copy the subtree once per invitee.
`items` names a datamodel path (signup.invitees, added to
../datamodel.json for this block); `item_as` binds a name that
exists only inside the body. Nothing offers that name in the
condition editor yet and js/proposed-core.js says why - a
deliberate deferral with a scope note, not a gap.
`index_as` is left unset: nothing in this body names the
position, and a key filled in to say 'unused' is noise.
The proposed core.subchart. `chart` stores the CHILD DOCUMENT's
id, which is the only chart identity a spike with no compiler
has; a compiler would emit the identity statifier-ex ADR-0052/
0057 defines instead. The picker that wrote this value offers
only the spike's own fixture documents (D11).
